σύν

[u^], old Att.ξύν; Boeot.σούν (Orchom. Boeot., iii B.C.): Prep. with dat. (rarely c. gen., ς. τῶν ἐν αὺτῷ νεκρῶν Mitteis (ii B.C.);

ς. ἡρώων (Phanagoria); ς. γυναικός ib. (Panticapaeum), cf. (ii A.D.), (vi A.D.)):—with. The form ξύν rarely occurs in , though it is not rare in compds. even when not required by the metre, as in ξυνέαξα, ξυνοχῇσιν, ξύμβλητο, ξύμπαντα; also uses ξύμπας, ξυνιέναι; in Ion. verse we find ξύν (but σύν), (perh. old Attic), but σύν, cf. ξυνωνίη, συνίημι; in early Ion. Prose (including Inscrr., cf. (Abu Simbel, vi B.C.), (Mylasa, iv B.C.), etc.) ξύν is only found in ξυνίημι, (cf. ἀξύνετος, ἀξυνεσίη, ξύνεσις), and in the phrase ξὺν νῷ (νόῳ codd.) , ; has only σύν, and in codd. ξύν has weaker authority than σύν (i p.cxxv Kuehlewein); in the late Ionic of , ξύν prevails over σύν; in Aeol. and Dor. it is rare, ξυνοίκην; ξυναλίαξε; elsewh. Dor.σύν, , (Locr., v B.C.), etc.; but in old Att. Inscrr. ξύν is the only form up to B.C.; σύν appears in v B.C. and becomes usual towards the end; after B.C. ξύν survives only in the formula γνώμην δὲ ξυμβάλλεσθαι κτλ.; the phrase ξὺν νῷ is found in , , , (σὺν); otherwise, of Att. Prose writers alone uses the preposition ξύν, and Lysias have ξυν- a few times in compds.; codd. have both ξυν- (, al.) and συν-; in , , , , and ξυν- is very freq.; in Trag. both forms occur. The Prep. σύν gradually gave way to μετά with gen., so that whereas has examples of σύν to of μετά with gen., the proportions in are of μετά to of σύν, in of μετά to of σύν, and in of μετά to of σύν: for these and other statistics see C. T. Mommsen, Beiträge zur Lehre von den griechischen Präpositionen (Frankfurt -): in Att. Prose and Com. σύν is restricted for the most part to signf. , and a few phrases, such as σὺν θεῷ, σὺν τ̔οῖς̓ ὅπλοις; Xenophon uses it freely, having examples to of μετά; in Pap., NT, and later Prose its use is much less restricted (v. infr.).

POSITION:—σύν sts. follows its case, , , . It freq. stands between Adj. and Subst., as , , etc.; more rarely between Subst. and Adj., , .

σύν AS ADV., together, at once, κενεὰς ς. Χεῖρας ἔχοντες; mostly folld. by δέ or τε, ς. δὲ πτερὰ πυκνὰ λίασθεν; ς. τε δύ' ἐρχομένω (cf. σύνδυο); ξ. τε διπλοῖ βασιλῆς (lyr.). It is sts. hard to distinguish this from tmesis, e.g. in ; so ξὺν κακῶς ποιεῖν is =Ξυγκακοποιεῖν in . In Old Testament Gr. it is sts. used to translate the Hebr. IN COMPO
with, along with, together, at the same time, hence of any kind of union, connexion, or participation in a thing, and metaph. of agreement or unity. In Compos. with a trans. Verb σύν may refer to the Object as well as the Subject, as συγκατακτείνειν may mean kill one person as well as another, or, join with another in killing.
of the completion of an action, altogether, completely, as in συνάγνυμι, συνασκέω, συνθρύπτω, συγκόπτω, συμπατέω, συμπληρόω, συντελέω, συντέμνω; sts., therefore, it seems only to strengthen the force of the simple word.
joined with numerals, σύνδυοtwo together, which sense often becomes distributive, by twos, two and two; so σύντρεις, σύμπεντε, etc., like Lat. bini, terni, etc.
σύν in Compos., before β μ π φ ψ, becomes συμ-; before γ κ ξ Χ, συγ-; before λ συλ-; before ς usu. συς-; but becomes συ- before ς followed by a conson. (e.g. συστῆναι), before ζ, and perh. sts. before ξ. In a poet. passage, ap., we have ξύμ alone in tmesi, ξύμ μοι λάβεσθε for συλλάβεσθέ μοι; cf. ὅτε ξὺμ πρῶτ' ἐφύοντο: in Inscrr. and Papyri these assimilations are freq. not found.
